name: Small Room
absorption: Moderate absorption from furniture, carpet, and soft furnishings. Short reflections arrive quickly, giving intimacy.

experiential.feel: close, contained, the world shrunk to arm's reach
prose_fragments: Sound stays close here — no room for echoes to develop, every noise direct and present.
The walls are near enough to catch everything and give it back quickly, dried of reverb.
An intimate acoustic — you hear the room's smallness in how quickly sound dies.

name: Large Hall
absorption: Hard floors and distant walls create long reflection paths. Sound blooms and lingers.

experiential.feel: grand, spacious, sound given room to breathe and expand
prose_fragments: Every sound unfolds twice — once direct, once returned from the far walls, softened and spread.
The hall adds its own voice to everything — a warm, rolling tail that follows each sound like a shadow.
Distance becomes audible. Close sounds are sharp; anything farther away arrives with the hall wrapped around it.

name: Cathedral
absorption: Stone walls, vaulted ceilings, minimal soft surfaces. Sound reverberates for seconds, each reflection adding to a shimmering tail.

experiential.feel: transcendent, vast, sound becoming something larger than its source
prose_fragments: Sound here doesn't end — it transforms. A single note becomes a chord as reflections layer upon reflections.
The stone holds everything, gives nothing back quickly. Every sound lingers, smeared across time.
You speak and your voice comes back to you changed — larger, older, as if the building has opinions about what you said.

name: Tiled Bathroom
absorption: Hard, reflective tiles on every surface. Small volume but long reverb. High frequencies ring sharply.

experiential.feel: bright, enclosed, everything amplified and reflected back at you
prose_fragments: The tiles turn every sound into a small performance — amplified, brightened, given a halo of reflection.
Your voice sounds better in here. That's the reverb. The hard surfaces flattering you with their reflections.
A small space that sounds large — the echo giving the illusion of more room than the walls allow.

name: Forest
absorption: Trees, leaves, and soft ground absorb and scatter sound in all directions. No flat reflective surfaces. Natural diffusion.

experiential.feel: hushed, scattered, sound absorbed into the living fabric of trees
prose_fragments: Sound here is swallowed by the trees — absorbed by bark and leaf and scattered into incoherence.
No echoes. The forest eats reflections. What you hear is direct sound only, stripped of all reverb.
An acoustic intimacy enforced by nature — the trees create a dry, close sound-world where nothing carries far.

name: Open Field
absorption: No reflective surfaces at all. Sound radiates outward and never returns. Pure inverse-square law.

experiential.feel: exposed, vast, sound dissolving into openness
prose_fragments: Sound leaves and doesn't come back. No walls, no ceiling, nothing to bounce off — just the air and distance.
Your voice sounds small out here. The field offers no acoustic support, no flattering reverb.
The purest acoustic — just source and air. What you hear is exactly what was made, without the room's commentary.

name: Underwater
absorption: Water transmits low frequencies efficiently but absorbs highs. Sound travels faster (4x) and direction becomes confused.

experiential.feel: enveloping, disorienting, sound arriving from everywhere and nowhere
prose_fragments: Everything is bass here — highs stripped away, the world reduced to low, muffled thuds and rumbles.
Sound travels differently through water — faster, from all directions, impossible to locate by ear alone.
A submerged acoustic, thick and directionless, every sound wrapped in the medium that carries it.

name: Cave
absorption: Hard rock walls, irregular surfaces creating complex reflection patterns. Long reverb, prominent flutter echoes.

experiential.feel: ancient, enclosed, sound bouncing off stone older than memory
prose_fragments: The cave multiplies everything — a single sound becomes a family of echoes, each one from a different wall.
Stone this old has been reflecting sound for millennia. Your footstep joins a history of echoes.
Flutter echoes ping back and forth between parallel rock faces, turning a handclap into a brief machine-gun burst.

name: Parking Garage
absorption: Concrete on every surface, large volume, flat parallel surfaces. Aggressive reverb, strong flutter echoes.

experiential.feel: industrial, harsh, every sound multiplied by concrete
prose_fragments: Concrete gives nothing — absorbs nothing, softens nothing. Every sound hits the walls and bounces back harder.
The flat parallel surfaces create flutter echoes that turn a car door slam into a rapid-fire burst.
A space designed for cars, not acoustics — and the sound knows it. Everything is too loud, too long, too much.

name: Library
absorption: Books absorb mid and high frequencies excellently. Carpet, soft chairs. The quietest designed space most people enter.

experiential.feel: hushed, padded, sound discouraged by design
prose_fragments: Books are excellent acoustic absorbers — a wall of them is like a wall of soft foam. The library knows this.
Sound is rationed here. Every noise feels louder because the baseline is so low.
The hush isn't just social convention — it's physics. The materials here conspire to make silence easy.

name: Busy Street
absorption: Buildings create a canyon effect, reflecting traffic noise back and forth. Ambient noise floor is high.

experiential.feel: loud, layered, a constant wash of urban noise competing for attention
prose_fragments: The buildings form a sound canyon — traffic noise bounces between facades, amplified by the geometry.
Everything competes. Engines, voices, footsteps, signals — a broadband wall of city sound.
Conversation requires raised voices. The street demands its acoustic tribute from everyone.

name: Subway Platform
absorption: Tile, concrete, metal — all hard, all reflective. The tunnel adds a long reverb tail and funnels wind noise.

experiential.feel: harsh, anticipatory, the acoustic prelude to a train arriving
prose_fragments: The tunnel acts as a waveguide — wind and rumble arrive before the train does, the space announcing what's coming.
Tile and concrete make every sound sharp and persistent. Voices blur into a general murmur.
When the train arrives, the platform becomes a compression chamber — noise levels jump 30 dB in seconds.

name: Concert Hall
absorption: Engineered for optimal reverb — diffusers, absorbers, and reflectors placed with precision. The gold standard of designed acoustics.

experiential.feel: lush, enveloping, sound treated with reverence by the architecture
prose_fragments: The hall was designed for this — every surface calculated to enhance, never to distort or mask.
Sound blooms here the way it's supposed to. Warm, full, present — with just enough reverb to add richness without blur.
The best seat in a great hall lets you hear details you'd miss anywhere else — the breath before the note, the room after.

name: Bedroom
absorption: Bed, curtains, carpet, clothes — all absorbers. A soft, quiet acoustic that encourages low volumes.

experiential.feel: soft, private, the most acoustically personal space in the house
prose_fragments: The softest room in the house. Fabric everywhere drinking up sound, making everything quieter, closer.
A whisper works here. The room is built for quiet conversations and sleep.
The clock, the breath, the rustle of sheets — in a bedroom, these small sounds become the soundtrack.

name: Kitchen
absorption: Hard surfaces — tile, metal, stone — with some absorption from soft goods. Bright, reflective, active acoustic.

experiential.feel: lively, bright, a working space that amplifies activity
prose_fragments: Hard surfaces make the kitchen acoustically bright — every clatter, clink, and sizzle amplified and crisped.
The kitchen doesn't soften anything. Pots ring, water splashes, timers beep — all with sharp clarity.
A working acoustic for a working room — nothing subtle, everything present.

name: Stairwell
absorption: Concrete or plaster walls, hard floors, vertical shaft creating a natural reverb chamber. Footsteps multiply dramatically.

experiential.feel: vertical, echoing, a space that amplifies footsteps into drama
prose_fragments: The vertical shaft acts as a reverb chamber — footsteps multiply into a cascading rhythm of echoes.
Voices spiral up the stairwell, arriving at the top changed — more reverberant, slightly mysterious.
Every floor you climb changes what you hear — the echo tail growing as the space above opens up.

name: Tunnel
absorption: Curved hard surfaces focus and guide sound. Extreme reverb, especially for low frequencies. Whisper galleries form naturally.

experiential.feel: enclosed, amplified, sound channeled and focused by the curved walls
prose_fragments: The tunnel focuses sound like a lens focuses light — channeling it, concentrating it, sending it farther than it should go.
Low frequencies thrive here — the curved walls act as a waveguide, bass building on itself.
A whisper at one end can arrive at the other intact — the tunnel's geometry defying distance.

name: Rooftop
absorption: Open sky above, one reflective surface below. A half-outdoor acoustic — some reflection from the roof surface, none from above.

experiential.feel: exposed, elevated, sound escaping upward into open air
prose_fragments: Half the sound goes up and never comes back. The sky absorbs everything you send it.
The roof surface gives a single reflection, then the sound is free — escaping upward into nothing.
City sounds rise to meet you here — traffic, sirens, voices — all softened by the distance below.

name: Recording Studio
absorption: Engineered for maximum absorption — acoustic foam, bass traps, diffusers. The most controlled acoustic humans build.

experiential.feel: controlled, clinical, sound isolated and examined under acoustic microscope
prose_fragments: The deadest room most people will ever enter. Every reflection killed, every resonance trapped.
Sound here is raw — no room sound, no reverb, no flattery. Just the source, naked.
The silence between sounds is absolute. No ambient, no hum, no room — just the absence of sound.

name: Gymnasium
absorption: Large volume, hard floors, high ceilings, metal structure. Everything echoes, nothing is absorbed.

experiential.feel: loud, chaotic, a space that amplifies every bounce and shout
prose_fragments: The gym turns every sound into a crowd — a single basketball bounce becomes a thunderclap of echoes.
Hard surfaces everywhere, huge volume — the acoustic equivalent of an amplifier with the gain too high.
Whistles shriek, shoes squeak, balls boom — each sound given a long, reverberant tail by the unforgiving space.

name: Car Interior
absorption: Tiny volume, mixed surfaces (glass, fabric, plastic). Very short reflections make everything present and close. Road noise provides constant low-frequency bed.

experiential.feel: enclosed, private, a moving room with its own acoustic signature
prose_fragments: The smallest room most people spend time in — everything is close, present, immediate.
Road noise provides a constant bass bed that makes silence impossible but conversation easy.
Music sounds different in a car — the small space and near walls create an accidental surround sound.

name: Small Church
absorption: Wood pews, stone or plaster walls, modest height. Warm reverb that flatters voices and acoustic instruments.

experiential.feel: warm, communal, an acoustic designed for shared listening
prose_fragments: The wooden pews add warmth, the stone walls add sustain — a balance of absorption and reflection that flatters the human voice.
Hymns were written for rooms like this — the reverb blending voices together, forgiving imprecision.
An acoustic that encourages congregation — individual voices merging into something larger than their parts.

name: Narrow Alley
absorption: Hard walls close together create strong early reflections. Sound bounces between parallel surfaces, creating flutter echo.

experiential.feel: compressed, intimate, sound squeezed between walls
prose_fragments: The alley presses sound between its walls like a vice — everything amplified, echoed, doubled.
Your footsteps come back at you from both sides, slightly delayed, as if someone is following.
Sound has no room to spread here. It goes up or it bounces back.

name: Tatami Room
absorption: Straw tatami, paper screens, and wooden frames absorb and diffuse mid-frequencies. Hushed and warm.

experiential.feel: hushed, warm, the acoustic of respect and restraint
prose_fragments: The tatami absorbs your footsteps, your voice, your urgency — everything is quieter here.
Paper walls and straw floors conspire to make every sound gentle.
A room designed for silence, where even a whisper feels like an intrusion.

name: Greenhouse
absorption: Glass walls reflect high frequencies. Plants absorb some mid-range. Humid air adds warmth.

experiential.feel: bright, humid, sound caught between glass and green
prose_fragments: Glass walls reflect your voice back crisp and bright, while the plants soften the edges.
The drip of condensation is amplified — each drop a clear note on glass or leaf.
Humid air makes everything feel close, including the sounds.

name: Wine Barrel Room
absorption: Curved wooden barrels scatter and warm the sound. Low frequencies resonate in the barrel cavities.

experiential.feel: warm, subterranean, aged wood humming with stored time
prose_fragments: The barrels hum sympathetically with every low sound — the room has its own bass note.
Wood absorbs the highs and returns the lows, warm and rounded, like the wine inside.
Your voice sounds richer in here. The barrels are doing you a favor.

name: Server Room
absorption: Raised floor, dropped ceiling, rows of equipment create a constant broadband fan noise floor.

experiential.feel: relentless, artificial, the hum of computation made audible
prose_fragments: The fans never stop — a broadband white noise that erases silence permanently.
You have to raise your voice to be heard over the machines thinking.
Cold air moves constantly, and with it a sound that is more vibration than noise.

name: Phone Booth
absorption: Extremely small volume. Sound has nowhere to go. Your voice fills the entire space immediately.

experiential.feel: claustrophobic, intimate, a coffin for conversation
prose_fragments: Your own breathing fills the booth. Your voice has nowhere to go but into the phone.
The glass walls show the world but the sound is all yours — a private acoustic island.
So small that speaking feels like shouting and whispering feels normal.

name: Treehouse
absorption: Open sides let sound escape into the canopy. Wood floor adds warmth. Elevated position changes what you hear.

experiential.feel: elevated, exposed, hearing the world from above
prose_fragments: Sound reaches you differently up here — birdsong is louder, ground sounds muffled by height.
The wooden platform creaks with every shift of weight, narrating your presence to the trees.
Wind is louder at this height, and it brings sounds from further away.

name: Igloo
absorption: Snow absorbs nearly everything. The most acoustically dead natural structure possible.

experiential.feel: buried, silent, the quietest room nature builds
prose_fragments: Snow absorbs everything — the igloo is the quietest room you've ever been in.
Sound dies instantly here. No echo, no reverb, just the close warmth of trapped air and snow walls.
The silence is so deep you hear your own blood moving.

name: Tent in Rain
absorption: Thin fabric membrane amplifies rain impact. Interior is small and soft. Rain becomes the dominant feature.

experiential.feel: sheltered, rhythmic, the thinnest possible barrier between you and the storm
prose_fragments: The rain on the tent is everything — a constant patter inches from your face, amplified by the taut fabric.
Inside the tent, the rain is a drum solo performed on your roof.
The fabric is the thinnest shelter imaginable, and the rain reminds you of that with every drop.

name: Hot Spring (Onsen)
absorption: Open air with stone surrounds. Steam absorbs high frequencies. Water provides constant background.

experiential.feel: warm, primal, sound softened by steam and stone
prose_fragments: Steam muffles everything — voices arrive soft and warm, stripped of their edges.
The constant gentle lap of water against stone is the baseline. Everything else floats on top.
Sound here is like the water: warm, unhurried, slightly blurred at the edges.
